props.gloss_en: one who reads the Megillah out of order has not fulfilled [his obligation]
Rava: the rule derives from 'according to their writing and according to their times' (Esth 9:27) -- as their times are not out of order, so their writing is not
rather, from 'and these days are remembered and done' (Esth 9:28): remembering is juxtaposed to doing -- as doing is not out of order, so remembering
it was taught: and so [out of order, one has not fulfilled] in Hallel
and so in the recitation of the Shema
and in Tefilla
Rabbah: from 'from the rising of the sun to its setting' (Ps 113:3)
Rav Yosef: from 'this is the day the Lord has made' (Ps 118:24)
Rav Avya: from 'may the name of the Lord be blessed' (Ps 113:2)
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak (some say Rav Acha bar Yaakov): from 'from now and forever' (Ps 113:2)
the Shema [is recited] as it is written -- Rebbi
and the Sages say: in any language
Rebbi's reason: the verse says 'and [these words] shall be' (Deut 6:6)
'vehayu' -- as they are, so shall they be
the Rabbis' reason: the verse says 'hear' (Deut 6:4)
'shema' -- in any language that you hear
'shema' is needed [by Rebbi] for: make audible to your ears what you utter with your mouth
the Rabbis hold like the one who says: one who recited the Shema and did not make it audible to his ear has fulfilled
'vehayu' is needed [by the Rabbis] for: that one not read out of order
Rebbi derives not-out-of-order from 'devarim' / 'hadevarim'
(entertained) Rebbi holds the whole Torah may be said in any language -- else why write 'vehayu'?
(entertained) the Rabbis hold the whole Torah must be said in the holy tongue -- else why write 'shema'?
Shimon HaPakuli arranged the eighteen blessings in order before Rabban Gamliel in Yavne
a hundred and twenty elders, among them several prophets, instituted the eighteen blessings in order
from where that one says [the blessing of] the Patriarchs? 'ascribe to the Lord, sons of the mighty' (Ps 29:1)
and gevurot? 'ascribe to the Lord glory and strength' (Ps 29:1)
and kedushot? 'ascribe to the Lord the glory of His name, bow to the Lord in the beauty of holiness' (Ps 29:2)
bina after kedusha: 'they shall sanctify the Holy One of Jacob' (Isa 29:23), and adjacent to it 'those who erred in spirit shall know understanding' (Isa 29:24)
teshuva after bina: 'and his heart will understand, and he will return and be healed' (Isa 6:10)
selicha after teshuva: 'let him return to the Lord and He will have mercy on him, and to our God, for He will abundantly forgive' (Isa 55:7)
another verse is written: 'who forgives all your iniquities, who heals all your diseases, who redeems your life from the pit' (Ps 103:3-4) -- redemption and healing come after forgiveness
Rava: since they are destined to be redeemed in the seventh, therefore they fixed it seventh
the master: in the sixth, sounds; in the seventh, wars; at the end of the seventh, the son of David comes
R' Acha: since circumcision, which needs healing, was given on the eighth, therefore they fixed healing eighth
R' Alexandri: the blessing of the years is ninth -- [it is said] against those who raise prices
as it is written 'break the arm of the wicked' (Ps 10:15), and when David said it, he said it in the ninth [psalm]
ingathering of exiles after the years: 'and you, mountains of Israel, give your branches and bear your fruit for My people Israel, for they are soon to come' (Ezek 36:8)
once the exiles are gathered, judgment is done on the wicked: 'I will turn My hand upon you and purge your dross' (Isa 1:25), and 'I will restore your judges as at first' (Isa 1:26)
and it is written [next]: 'and I will restore your judges as at first' (Isa 1:26)
once judgment is done on the wicked, the transgressors cease: 'and the destruction of transgressors and sinners together' (Isa 1:28)
and he includes the zedim with them [in the same blessing]
once the transgressors cease, the horn of the righteous is raised: 'all the horns of the wicked I will cut off; the horns of the righteous shall be lifted' (Ps 75:11)
and he includes the righteous converts with the righteous: 'rise before the hoary head and honour the elder' (Lev 19:32), and adjacent to it 'and if a stranger sojourns with you' (Lev 19:33)
where is their horn raised? in Jerusalem: 'ask for the peace of Jerusalem; those who love you shall prosper' (Ps 122:6)
once Jerusalem is built, David comes: 'afterward the children of Israel shall return and seek the Lord their God and David their king' (Hos 3:5)
once David comes, prayer comes: 'I will bring them to My holy mountain and gladden them in My house of prayer' (Isa 56:7)
once prayer comes, the [Temple] service comes: 'their burnt-offerings and sacrifices shall be accepted on My altar' (Isa 56:7)
once the service comes, thanksgiving comes: 'whoever sacrifices a thanks-offering honours Me' (Ps 50:23)
birkat kohanim after hodaah: 'and Aaron lifted his hands toward the people and blessed them, and came down from offering the sin-offering, the burnt-offering and the peace-offerings' (Lev 9:22)

sim shalom after birkat kohanim: 'and they shall place My name upon the children of Israel and I will bless them' (Num 6:27); the Holy One's blessing is peace -- 'the Lord will bless His people with peace' (Ps 29:11)
the blessing of the Holy One, blessed be He, is peace, as it is said: 'the Lord will bless His people with peace' (Ps 29:11)
from here on it is forbidden to recount the praise of the Holy One, blessed be He
R' Elazar: 'who can utter the mighty acts of the Lord, proclaim all His praise?' (Ps 106:2) -- for whom is it fitting to utter the Lord's mighty acts? for one who can proclaim all His praise
R' Yochanan: one who recounts the praise of the Holy One excessively is uprooted from the world -- 'shall it be told Him when I speak? if a man says it, he is swallowed up' (Job 37:20)
R' Yehuda of Kfar Gibboraya: 'to You silence is praise' (Ps 65:2) -- the remedy of all is silence
they say in the West: a word for a sela, silence for two

והקדישו את קדוש יעקב (Isa 29:23), וסמיך ליה וידעו תועי רוח בינה (29:24) -- understanding is placed after holiness
מפני שיבה תקום והדרת פני זקן (Lev 19:32), וסמיך ליה וכי יגור אתכם גר (19:33) -- converts are included with the righteous

supports.gloss_en: דאמר רבי אלעזר: למי נאה למלל גבורות ה' -- למי שיכול להשמיע כל תהלתו (kind svara: no support kind names an amoraic dictum adduced with דאמר)

objections.gloss_en: מידי קריאה כתיבה הכא? עשייה כתיבה -- 'according to their writing' concerns the doing of the days, not reading; unanswered: the stam replaces the source (אלא מהכא)
ורבי נמי, הא כתיב שמע? -- for Rebbi too 'shema' is written, which the Rabbis read as 'any language you hear'

answered_by.gloss_en: ההוא מיבעי ליה: השמע לאזניך מה שאתה מוציא מפיך (= p_shema_hashma)

objections.gloss_en: ורבנן נמי, הכתיב והיו? -- for the Rabbis too 'vehayu' is written, which Rebbi reads as 'as they are'

answered_by.gloss_en: ההוא מיבעי ליה שלא יקרא למפרע (= p_vehayu_lemafrea)

objections.gloss_en: וכי מאחר דמאה ועשרים זקנים ומהם כמה נביאים תקנו תפלה על הסדר, שמעון הפקולי מאי הסדיר?

answered_by.gloss_en: שכחום, וחזר וסדרום -- they were forgotten, and he arranged them again

objections.gloss_en: אי הכי -- לימא רפואה בתרה דתשובה? (ושב ורפא לו)

answered_by.gloss_en: לא סלקא דעתך, דכתיב וישוב אל ה' וירחמהו... כי ירבה לסלוח -- forgiveness follows repentance (= p_selicha_achar_teshuva)

objections.gloss_en: ומאי חזית דסמכת אהא? סמוך אהא! -- what did you see to rely on this [verse]? rely on that one! (Steinsaltz: on ושב ורפא לו)

answered_by.gloss_en: כתב קרא אחרינא: הסולח לכל עוניכי הרופא לכל תחלואיכי הגואל משחת חייכי (= p_geula_refua_achar_selicha)

objections.gloss_en: למימרא דגאולה ורפואה בתר סליחה היא? והכתיב ושב ורפא לו!

answered_by.gloss_en: ההוא לאו רפואה דתחלואים היא, אלא רפואה דסליחה היא -- that healing is the healing of forgiveness

objections.gloss_en: והאמר מר: בששית קולות, בשביעית מלחמות, במוצאי שביעית בן דוד בא -- the redemption comes after the seventh, not in it (kind svara under protest: no kind for והאמר)

answered_by.gloss_en: מלחמה נמי אתחלתא דגאולה היא -- war too is the beginning of redemption

objections.gloss_en: אימא קודם עבודה? -- say [birkat kohanim] before the avoda [blessing]! (Steinsaltz: the verse seems to have Aaron bless and then go down to sacrifice)

answered_by.gloss_en: לא סלקא דעתך, דכתיב וירד מעשת החטאת -- מי כתיב לעשות? מעשות כתיב: he came down FROM offering

objections.gloss_en: ולימרה אחר העבודה! -- then say it immediately after the avoda blessing

answered_by.gloss_en: לא סלקא דעתך, דכתיב זובח תודה (= p_hodaah_achar_avoda)

objections.gloss_en: מאי חזית דסמכת אהאי, סמוך אהאי! -- what did you see to rely on this [verse]? rely on that one! (Steinsaltz: why let Ps 50:23 place hodaah after avoda rather than Lev 9:22 place birkat kohanim there)

answered_by.gloss_en: מסתברא: עבודה והודאה חדא מילתא היא -- it stands to reason: service and thanksgiving are one matter
